either an older client or one that cannot. That is a distinct state from a
run reporting zeroes, and the interface must render it as unknown rather than
as a stalled run.

Every byte figure here is cumulative since the run started, exactly as
reported; [`Self::bytes_per_second`] is the only derived rate.

bytes_cached.description: Bytes found already present, and so not re-uploaded.

bytes_estimated.description:
Total bytes the run currently expects to handle. An estimate the run may
revise upward, so a percentage derived from it can go down.

bytes_per_second.description:
Upload rate over the trailing window, derived by differencing cumulative
`bytes_uploaded` across samples. `None` when the window holds fewer than
two samples, spans no time, or the run reports no uploaded figure — never
zero as a stand-in, since "not enough data to say" and "moving no bytes"
are different answers.

current_path.description: What the run was working on at the last sample.

extra.description:
Whatever the backup engine reported beyond what Canopy models, verbatim
from the last sample. Shown for inspection; never interpreted.

files_estimated.description: Total files the run currently expects to handle.

ignored_errors.description: Errors hit and deliberately ignored so far.

observed_at.description: When the last sample arrived, as timed by Canopy on receipt.

s3_received_payload_bytes.description: Payload bytes received from object storage so far.

s3_received_raw_bytes.description: Raw bytes received from object storage so far.

s3_sent_payload_bytes.description: Payload bytes sent to object storage so far.

s3_sent_raw_bytes.description: Raw bytes sent to object storage so far, as the client's proxy tallied.

seconds_since_observed.description:
How long since the last sample. The "is anyone still there" figure: it
grows without bound if a device goes quiet mid-run.

LiveVersionsBracket.description:
The lowest and highest software version currently reported by any
production server.

max.description: Newest version currently reported by a production server.

min.description: Oldest version currently reported by a production server.

Machine.description:
A host in the fleet: a box, physical or virtual, that canopy monitors.

Distinct from the application server running on it. A machine carries the
facts that belong to the box — where it is, what identity speaks for it,
how long it may be silent — so a host running two workloads reports its
platform, memory and filesystems once rather than once per workload.

A machine hosts any number of applications, including none: one created but
not yet reporting presents as awaiting check-in rather than as an error.

alert_when_down_for.description:
How long this machine may go without reporting before it is considered
unreachable. Only enforced while `is_monitored`; the value is kept
while unmonitored so turning monitoring back on does not lose it.

cloud.description: Whether this machine is hosted in the cloud, if known.

deleted_at.description:
When set, the machine is archived: out of the live fleet, with its
record and history retained. Archiving a machine archives the
applications on it.

device_id.description:
The identity that authenticates this machine, if one is enrolled. A
machine has at most one, and an identity belongs to at most one
machine, so resolving either from the other is unambiguous.

oneOf.description: Where this machine is, if known.

group_id.description:
The group this machine belongs to. The one thing an operator supplies
when creating a machine: which group a box belongs to is the one
fact the box has no way of knowing. The applications on it take it.

is_monitored.description:
Whether this machine is actively monitored. Switching it off quiets
the machine's own checks and does not touch the applications on it —
a box excused from monitoring says nothing about its workloads.

name.description:
The name its operator gave it. Distinct from the hostname the
operating system reports, which is a reported figure rather than a
field an operator sets.

notes.description: Free-form operator notes about this machine.

registered_at.description:
When an identity completed enrolment for this machine. While `None`,
the machine is awaiting its first check-in.

Also the anchor a backup deadline counts from, which is why it belongs
to the machine: anchoring on an application's registration would
restart a box's backup clock every time a workload was added to it.

restore_allowed_by.description: Who opened the current restore window (Tailscale login), if any.

restore_allowed_until.description:
Until when this machine is allowed to mint restore credentials for
itself (ad-hoc `bestool canopy restore`). An operator opens this window
and it auto-expires; `None` (or a past instant) means restores are not
currently allowed. Restores read the group's backup repo, so they are
gated behind this deliberate, time-boxed opt-in rather than always
available.

A restore rewrites the box, so the window belongs to the box: a machine
carrying two workloads is opened once and restored once.

tags.description:
Key/value tags for this machine. A check filed against a machine is
graded by policy against these rather than against any application's.
An application's type is not among them, not being a property of a box.

machine_id.description:
The box to operate on. Backups are a machine's, so this names the box
rather than a workload on it.

MachineBackupCapabilityView.description:
One backup type a server has advertised support for, whether the operator
has enabled it, and its most recent activity. Enabling a capability is
what makes the server eligible for issued backup credentials and
scheduled runs of that type.

enabled.description:
Whether the operator has enabled scheduled backups of this type for
this server.

latest_snapshot_bytes.description: Bytes uploaded by that run, if reported.

latest_snapshot_id.description:
Identifier of this server and type's most recent successful backup,
if any.

machine_id.description: The server this capability belongs to.

next_backup_at.description:
When this server's next backup of this type is expected: the server's own
last success plus the effective interval, or "now" (overdue) if it's
scheduled but has never succeeded. `None` for disabled or manual-only
(no-interval) types. Per-server, so a lagging member isn't masked by a
freshly-backed-up sibling.

processing_since.description:
`Some(issued_at)` when a backup of this type appears to be in flight:
backup credentials were issued and are still valid, and no run has
been reported since they were issued. `None` otherwise. Lets the UI
show a "backing up…" state.

oneOf.description:
Live figures for the in-flight run of this type, when it is reporting
progress. `None` when nothing is in flight, or when the run reports no
progress — which is unknown, not zero.

type.description: Backup type this capability describes.

MachineCreateArgs.description:
What an operator supplies when adding a machine.

The group is the only field that matters to get right up front: which
group a box belongs to is the one thing the box has no way of knowing.

alert_when_down_for.description:
How long the box may be silent before it is unreachable, in seconds.
Defaults to the column's own default.

cloud.description: Whether the box is cloud-hosted, if known.

oneOf.description: Where the box is, if known.

group_id.description: The group this machine belongs to. The applications on it take it.

is_monitored.description: Whether the machine's own checks alert. Defaults to on.

name.description:
What to call the box. Distinct from the hostname its operating system
reports, which arrives as a reported figure.

notes.description: Operator notes shown on the machine's page.

oneOf.description: Operator-set tags. Reserved names are refused, as they are on an edit.

tailscale_identifier.description:
A tailnet node to bind this machine to up front, by address, node key,
or DNS name. Omit to enrol the machine later.

The operator is describing a box they can already see on the tailnet,
so binding it here saves an enrolment round trip. The identity is a
machine's, not an application's: the applications on the box are
reported and carry no identity of their own.

applications.description:
The applications on this machine. Empty for a machine that has been
created but has not yet reported: that is awaiting check-in, not an
error.

MachineDetail.description: A machine together with the applications running on it.

MachineDetailData.description:
Everything a machine's own page presents.

The machine's record, what the box reports about itself, its own health and
checks, the identity it authenticates with, and the applications running on
it. An application's version and database engine are not here: those are the
workload's, and each application carries its own (see [APP]).

applications.description:
The applications running on this box, each carrying its own
reachability and health so the page renders a dot per workload.

billing_labels.description:
The machine's effective `billing.*` labels — the ones Canopy hands its
device. A machine carries no product, a box not being a piece of
software.

checks.description: The machine's own checks across every source, graded and classified.

oneOf.description: Full detail on the identity bound to this machine, if it has enrolled.

figures.description:
What the box reports about itself, resolved across every source
reporting on it: platform, hardware, addresses, uptime.

oneOf.description:
The group this machine belongs to, with its notes and tags, so the page
renders its group section without a second fetch.

group_applications.description:
Every application in this box's group, for the tree the page ends with.
Empty when the machine is ungrouped. The applications on this box are
among them, the tree being a map of the group rather than of elsewhere.

group_machines.description:
Every machine in this box's group, for the same tree. Empty when the
machine is ungrouped.

health.description:
The machine's own health, from the checks filed against it. What the
applications on it make of their own checks is each application's.

last_reported_at.description: When the box last reported anything, across every source.

maintained.description:
Whether a maintenance window suspends this machine, its own or its
group's.

maintenance_settling.description: Whether the suspension is only the settle period.

munin.description:
Whether the box is known to run Munin, from the most recent source to
report the flag. Munin watches the box rather than anything running on
it, so the flag and the link it drives are the machine's.

operators.description:
The people logged in to this box right now, from its `external_users`
check. Empty unless the box is currently reporting: a stale report
cannot say who is on it now.

up.description: Whether the box is currently reporting, on its own threshold.

machine_id.description: The machine to operate on.

MachineScopeArgs.description: Request body identifying a machine to look up silences for.

machine_id.description: The machine to look up silences for.

MachineSilencedRef.description:
A silenced issue reference scoped to a single machine: issues matching this
`(source, ref)` on this box are still recorded, but are excluded from
incidents and notifications.

A box's own checks are the subject here — a full disk, a drifting clock —
not those of the applications running on it, which are silenced against
each application.

created_by.description: The operator who created this silence. `None` if not recorded.

machine_id.description: The machine this silence applies to.

ref.description: The issue reference this silence matches.

source.description: The issue source this silence matches.

MachineUpdateArgs.description:
Fields to change on a machine. Omitted fields are left alone; for the
nullable ones an explicit `null` clears the value.

alert_when_down_for.description: How long the machine may be silent before it is unreachable, in seconds.

cloud.description: New value for whether the box is cloud-hosted, or `null` to clear it.

oneOf.description: New location for the box, or `null` to clear it.

group_id.description:
New group, or `null` to remove it from its current one. The
applications on this machine move with it.

is_monitored.description:
New monitored state. Switching it off quiets the machine's own checks
and leaves the applications on it alone.

machine_id.description: The machine to edit.

name.description: New name for the box, or `null` to clear it.

notes.description: New free-form operator notes for the box.

oneOf.description: New set of key/value tags. Replaces the whole set.

MaintenanceKind.description:
Which maintenance cycle a reported backup-repository maintenance run
performed.

MaintenanceWindow.description: A declaration that a machine or a group is being worked on.

amended_at.description: When the window was last amended.

amended_by.description: The operator who last amended the window, where one has.

declared_by.description: The operator who declared the window. `None` if not recorded.

ended_at.description: When the window stopped holding. `None` while it holds.

ended_by.description:
The operator who lifted the window. `None` where its expected end
passed instead.

expected_end.description:
When the operator expects the work to finish. A window reaching it
ends itself.

machine_id.description:
Set for a window over one machine, covering the machine's own checks
and those of every application running on it.

note.description: What is being done, where the operator said.

server_group_id.description:
Set for a window over a group, covering the group's own checks and
those of every machine in it.

settled_at.description:
Stamped once the settle period has elapsed and the target's issues
have been re-evaluated.

updated_at.description: When this record was last modified.

ManagedZoneView.description:
A DNS zone Canopy can write records in.

Zones come from the Canopy instance's own configuration rather than from operator
state: they are what the infrastructure has granted Canopy write access to,
and they bound which domains a group can be given.

apex.description: The zone's apex domain, for example `tamanu.app`.

provider_zone_id.description: The identifier the DNS provider knows this zone by.

server_group_id.description:
The group to ask about. Null for a server with no group, which can hold
no domain and so no useful grant.

McpTokenView.description:
Metadata about an MCP access token. Never includes the secret value
itself — that's only ever returned once, at minting time.

created_by.description: The login of the admin who minted this token.

expires_at.description:
When the token stops being accepted. Tokens are valid for one year
from minting; there is no way to request a different lifetime.

last_used_at.description:
When the token was last used to authenticate, or `null` if it has
never been used. May lag the true last use by up to a minute.

name.description: Operator-chosen label for what the token is used for.

revoked_at.description: When the token was revoked, or `null` if it has not been revoked.

MergeIntoArgs.description: Request to merge two device records into one.

source_id.description:
The device to merge away — usually the automatically-discovered,
tailnet-only device that doesn't yet have its own certificate
key. This device is removed once the merge completes.

target_id.description:
The device that remains after the merge — usually the existing
device that already owns the server attachment and connection
history.

MinorVersionGroup.description:
A group of versions sharing the same major.minor release line, with a
summary of the line's overall readiness.

count.description: Number of patch versions in this release line.

first_created_at.description:
Creation time of the first (patch 0) published version in this
release line. Falls back to the earliest published patch, or the
current time, if patch 0 hasn't been published.

last_created_at.description:
Creation time of the latest published patch in this release line,
or the current time if nothing has been published yet.

latest_patch.description:
Highest published patch number in this release line, or 0 if none
are published yet.

major.description: Major version number for this release line.

minor.description: Minor version number for this release line.

ready.description:
`true` when the latest published patch in this release line is
itself ready. An old, since-fixed issue on an earlier patch doesn't
dim the whole release line. Also `true` when nothing has been
published yet.

versions.description: All versions in this release line, patch descending.

MintArgs.description: Request body for minting a new MCP access token.

name.description:
Operator-chosen label, e.g. which agent will hold this token. Cannot
be empty or only whitespace.

MintedToken.description:
The result of minting a new MCP access token: its metadata plus the
one-time secret value. This is the only response that will ever include
the secret.

secret.description: The bearer token itself. Shown once; never retrievable again.

token.description: Metadata about the newly minted token.

NameView.description: A name a server has registered, and how far Canopy has got with it.

addresses.description: The addresses the server asked to be reachable at.

last_error.description: Why the last publish attempt failed, if it did.

name.description: The name, normalised.

published.description: Whether the zone has caught up with what the server asked for.

published_addresses.description:
The addresses Canopy has actually published. Differs from `addresses`
while a change is waiting to be reconciled.

published_at.description: When Canopy last published this name's records.

zone.description:
Apex of the managed zone covering this name, or null where no configured
zone does — in which case Canopy can publish nothing for it.

NamespaceRef.description:
A namespace on the wire, as the pair of fields it is stored as.

The private API names a check by source, namespace and name, so this is
what a request carries and what a listing returns alongside the
presentational qualified form. It mirrors the storage columns rather than
inventing a third encoding, so a row read out of a listing goes straight
back into a mutation.

application_type.description:
The application type, set when and only when `subject` is
`application`.

subject.description:
`machine`, `application`, or `null` for a curated source, whose names
are unqualified.

OpenWindow.description:
An open window with the target it covers, named so a fleet-wide view
reads without a lookup per row.

target.description: The target as it reads to an operator.

OperatorPresence.description:
One person currently connected to a server, identified by their
Tailscale login.

Only sessions that could be tied to an authenticated Tailscale identity
are reported here — local console access and other unauthenticated
sessions don't produce one of these. A person with several simultaneous
sessions appears once.

connected_since.description:
When the person's current connection began. If they have multiple
simultaneous sessions, this is the earliest start time among them.

login.description: The person's Tailscale login (an email address).

name.description:
The person's display name, if known. `None` if this login has never
been seen before.

profile_pic.description: URL of the person's profile picture, if known.

Page_BestoolSnippetInfo.description: A single page of a paginated list response.

items.description:
Summary of a saved SQL snippet, as shown when listing the snippet
library.

description.description: Optional description of what the snippet does.

id.description: Unique identifier for this version of the snippet.

name.description: The snippet's display name.

total.description:
The total number of items across all pages, not just this one — use
this to render page counts without a separate request.

Page_DeviceInfo.description: A single page of a paginated list response.

items.description:
Full record for a device: its identity and role, every authentication
key ever registered on it, its most recent connection, and a live
Tailscale snapshot when one is available.

device.description: Core identity, role, and Tailscale attachment for the device.

keys.description: Every authentication key ever registered on this device, active or not.

oneOf.description: The most recent connection seen from this device, if any.

Live snapshot from the Tailscale network for a device that's
currently attached to a tailnet node. Omitted if the device has
no tailnet attachment, the tailnet directory integration isn't
configured, or the node isn't found in the directory's cache.

total.description:
The total number of items across all pages, not just this one — use
this to render page counts without a separate request.

Page_ServerInfo.description: A single page of a paginated list response.

items.description:
A server in the fleet inventory: its identity, classification, network
address, monitoring configuration, and (when requested by the endpoint)
current reachability/health.

alert_when_down_for.description:
Threshold in seconds for the reachability sweep to consider this
server down. Always positive; only consulted when `is_monitored`
is `true`. The default at creation is 600 (10 minutes).

cloud.description: Whether this server runs in a cloud environment, if known.

display_host.description:
Effective URL for display: the stored `host`, or `https://{tailnet
hostname}` when the server has no URL but runs on a machine bound to a
Tailscale device, else an empty string.

oneOf.description: Geographic location of the server, if known.

group_id.description: The group this server belongs to, if any.

group_name.description:
Display name of the group this server belongs to, included directly so
list views don't need a separate lookup. `None` if ungrouped.

oneOf.description:
Self-reported health from the most recent status report. Same
omitted-vs-present semantics as `up`.

host.description: The server's stored URL, if any. May be absent for device-only applications.

is_monitored.description:
Whether canopy is actively watching this server. When `false`, the
reachability sweep skips it and its issues don't contribute to
incidents.

machine_id.description:
The machine this application runs on. Maintenance is declared over the
machine, so a surface offering to declare one needs it (see MNT).

maintained.description:
Whether a maintenance window suspends this server, its own or its
group's. Set alongside `up` and `health` by the endpoints that
decorate listings; `None` where they aren't.

may_manage_dns.description:
Whether the server may manage its own DNS records for names under its
group's domains.

may_manage_tls.description:
Whether the server may obtain TLS certificates for names under its
group's domains.

name.description: Operator-assigned name for the server, if any.

notes.description: Free-text operator notes about the server.

public_name.description:
Name this server appears under in the public mobile-app server list.
`None` means the server is not listed publicly.

oneOf.description:
Where this server sits in its group's promotion order (e.g.
production vs. staging), if applicable.

registered_at.description:
When a device completed enrollment for this server. `None` while
awaiting first check-in, at which point setup instructions still apply.

tags.description: Arbitrary operator-defined key/value labels attached to the server.

type.description:
What this application is: the software and the role it plays together.
Decides which of Canopy's per-application features apply to it.

oneOf.description:
Reachability of the server, derived from its most recent status
report. Omitted when the endpoint that produced this response didn't
batch-fetch statuses (e.g. the cheap list/get endpoints); a present
value of "gone" means the lookup ran and found no status at all.

total.description:
The total number of items across all pages, not just this one — use
this to render page counts without a separate request.

Page_SqlHistoryEntry.description: A single page of a paginated list response.

items.description: One entry in the shared history of queries run in the SQL playground.

id.description: Unique identifier for this history entry.

query.description: The SQL text that was executed.

tailscale_user.description: Tailscale login of the user who ran the query.

total.description:
The total number of items across all pages, not just this one — use
this to render page counts without a separate request.

PaginationArgs.description: Pagination window for a paged listing endpoint.

limit.description:
Maximum number of items to return. Endpoints that use this type
apply their own default when omitted.

offset.description: Number of items to skip from the start of the result set.

ParamType.description:
The data type of a restore-replica configuration parameter, which
determines how its value is validated. `duration` and `bytes` values must
be non-negative integers (a count of seconds and of bytes, respectively);
`integer` accepts any whole number, positive or negative; `boolean` is a
JSON boolean; `text` is a JSON string.

PartialServerGroup.description:
Fields to update on an existing server group. Only the fields present
are changed; omitted fields are left as-is.

name.description: New display name for the group.

notes.description: New free-form operator notes for the group.

slack_close_delay.description: New incident linger window, in seconds.

slack_open_delay.description: New incident-opened notification delay, in seconds.

oneOf.description:
New set of key/value tags shared by every server in the group. This
replaces the whole tag set.

PastPlan.description: One plan that has closed, in the fleet's plan history.

group_id.description: The group it was for.

group_name.description: Its name, so the view reads without a second lookup.

target_version.description: Where the plan was going, as semver.

PauseArgs.description: Why a server is being paused.

reason.description: Why, recorded so whoever finds the pause later knows what it was for.

PendingRequestRow.description: A pending one-off backup or restore request.

machine_id.description: The box the request is for.

purpose.description:
Why this run was requested: `backup` to write new data, or `restore`
to read existing data.

requested_by.description:
Identity of the operator who made the request (Tailscale login), if
known.

type.description: Backup type requested.

PlanOutcome.description: How a plan stands: still where the group is going, or the way it closed.

PlannableVersion.description: A version a group could be planned onto.

ready.description:
Whether it is clear of unresolved known issues, the same gate that keeps
a version off the public listings. A flagged version is still offered:
the issue may be resolved well before the planned date.

PlannedUpgrade.description: One row of the planned-upgrades view.

oneOf.description:
Whether a restore attempt is under way, carried beside the verdict rather
than folded into it: a restore takes hours, so a group mid-test would
otherwise read as untested for the whole window.

current_version.description: The version the group runs now, where it has reported one.

group_id.description: The group this concerns.

group_name.description: Its name, so the view reads without a second lookup.

late.description:
Whether the planned date has passed without the upgrade happening.
Presentational: a slipping upgrade is normal operational reality.

oneOf.description: The plan, absent for a group with none.

testable.description:
Whether anything is declared to migrate this group's data. A plan on a
group with nothing declared is never dispatched, so its verdict would sit
at "not tested" indefinitely with nothing on its way. `null` without a
plan.

verdict.description:
Where the group's data stands against the planned version, rolled up from
its applications: any failure makes the group a failure, since one server
whose data breaks is enough to stop the upgrade. `null` without a plan.

PlansForGroupArgs.description:
Request body for reading one group's plans. Named apart from the
migration-test one because utoipa keys component schemas by short name.

group_id.description: The group to read.

ProbeArgs.description: Request to inspect a bucket/prefix before configuring backups on it.

bucket.description: Name of the S3 bucket to inspect.

maintenance_role_arn.description:
AWS IAM role ARN to assume for the inspection (requires full read
access).

prefix.description:
Key prefix within the bucket to inspect; defaults to empty (bucket
root).

region.description: AWS region the bucket is in, if known.

target_role_arn.description:
AWS IAM role ARN to additionally validate for device use (checked in
both directions with a read-only no-op). Optional; supplying it lets
the setup wizard catch a role configuration problem before saving,
rather than when a device first attempts a backup.

ProbeResponse.description:
Result of inspecting a bucket/prefix: what's currently stored there, and
whether Canopy already has a configuration for it.

already_configured.description:
The server group already configured for this exact bucket and prefix,
if any.

error.description:
Present when `state` is `inaccessible`: a description of the failure
encountered while trying to access the bucket.

object_sample.description: A few example object keys found, when `state` is `other_content`.

state.description:
What was found at the inspected location: empty, an existing backup
repository, other (non-backup) content, or inaccessible.

ProblemDetailsSchema.description:
Standard error response body, returned for every non-2xx response.

This follows the RFC 7807 "Problem Details" shape: a stable machine-readable
`type`, a short `title`, the repeated HTTP `status` code, and an optional
`detail` string with specifics of this particular occurrence.

detail.description:
Human-readable explanation specific to this occurrence of the
problem, if any extra detail is available.

status.description: HTTP status code of the response, repeated here for convenience.

title.description:
Short, human-readable summary of the problem type. Does not vary
between occurrences of the same `type`.

type.description:
A URI reference identifying the problem type. Stable across
occurrences of the same error, so callers can match on it.

ProvisionArgs.description: Request to mint a new device credential.

device_id.description:
Attach the new credential to this existing device instead of
creating a new one. When omitted, a new device is created at
`role`.

key_name.description: Display name for the new key. Defaults to "Provisioned key".

role.description: Role to trust the device at.

ProvisionedCredential.description:
The one-time result of provisioning a device credential. The plaintext
private key lives only inside `key_age_base64`; Canopy never persists it.

device_id.description: The device the credential was issued for.

filename.description: Suggested filename for the downloaded encrypted key.

fingerprint.description:
Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the stored public key, to correlate the
credential with the device's key list.

key_age_base64.description:
Base64 (standard) of the age-encrypted PKCS#8 PEM private key. Decrypt
with `passphrase` (e.g. `bestool crypto reveal`) to recover the PEM.

key_id.description: Unique identifier for the newly-created key record.

passphrase.description:
Freshly-generated passphrase that decrypts `key_age_base64`. Share it
out-of-band, on a separate channel from the file.

ReachabilityMode.description:
How a source's silence bears on its servers' reachability.

Stored as text in Postgres, validated as this enum at the edges.

RecentRun.description:
One row of the recent-runs view: either a device-reported [`BackupRun`] or a
run inferred from a [`BackupCredentialIssuance`] that never matched a report.
Duration, when present, is Canopy-measured wall-clock — the interval from the
run's first credential issuance (its start) to its report (its end) — not a
client-reported figure.

at.description:
The row's effective time for sorting and display: `reported_at` when
reported, otherwise `started_at`.

bytes_uploaded.description: Bytes the device reported uploading, if any (reported runs only).

duration_seconds.description:
Canopy-measured run duration in seconds (report time minus first-issuance
time). `None` for an in-flight/unreported row or a run with no matching
issuance.

error.description: Error detail for a failed reported run, if any.

key.description:
Stable identity for UI keying: `run-<uuid>` for a reported run, or
`issuance-<id>` for an inferred attempt.

machine_id.description: The server this run was for, if known.

oneOf.description: The reported outcome; only present when `status` is `reported`.

Live figures for a run still in flight, from the progress it has reported.
`None` when the run has reported none — which is unknown, not zero.

purpose.description: Whether the run was a backup or a restore.

reported_at.description: When the device reported the run. `None` for an inferred (unreported) row.

run_id.description:
The run identifier, when known — present on a reported run, and on an
inferred row whose credential issuance carried one. Needed to fetch the
run's progress series; `None` for an issuance from a client that predates
run correlation, which therefore has no series to fetch.

s3_received_payload_bytes.description: Payload bytes received from S3 during the run, if tallied (reported runs only).

s3_received_raw_bytes.description: Raw bytes received from S3 during the run, if tallied (reported runs only).

s3_sent_payload_bytes.description: Payload bytes sent to S3 during the run, if tallied (reported runs only).

s3_sent_raw_bytes.description: Raw bytes sent to S3 during the run, if tallied (reported runs only).

snapshot_id.description:
Snapshot the run produced (backup) or used (restore), if any (reported
runs only).

snapshot_logical_bytes.description:
Logical size of the run's snapshot, if known (reported runs only). For
a backup this comes from repo inspection. For a restore it is resolved
from the backup run that produced the snapshot (matched by snapshot id),
falling back to inspection's backfill onto the restore run itself.

snapshot_taken_at.description:
When the run froze the data it captured, if it reported that. Distinct from
`reported_at`: for a long backup the two are hours apart, and this is the
one that says how old the data actually is.

started_at.description:
When the run started, taken from its first matching credential issuance.
`None` when no issuance could be matched (e.g. a run predating issuance
recording).

status.description: Whether this row is reported, in-flight, or an unreported past attempt.

type.description: The backup type that ran.

RecordArgs.description: Request body for recording where a group is going.

group_id.description: The group that intends to move.

note.description: Anything the next reader needs to know. Optional.

planned_end_time.description:
The hour the window closes, as `HH:MM`. Optional, and needs a start.
Earlier than the start means the following morning.

planned_for.description: The day it is expected to happen, as `YYYY-MM-DD`. Optional.

planned_time.description:
The hour it starts on that day, as `HH:MM`. Optional, and needs a day
and a zone.

planned_zone.description:
The IANA zone the planned time is a wall clock in, such as
`Pacific/Fiji`. Required alongside a time.

target_version_id.description: The published version it intends to move to.

ciphertext_base64.description:
A single-use verification challenge encrypted to the recovery
recipients, base64-encoded. The operator decrypts this offline with a
held private key (any tool that supports the `age` encryption format)
and submits the decrypted plaintext to the `/backups/recovery_verify`
endpoint to prove the key is genuinely held.

recipients.description:
The recovery recipients (age public keys) this challenge was
encrypted to.

RecoveryStatusResponse.description:
Status of the disaster-recovery verification ceremony: whether recovery
is configured, and whether a fresh verification is due.

configured.description: Whether recovery recipients are configured on this server at all.

due.description: Whether a fresh verification ceremony is due.

last_verified_at.description: When the recovery ceremony was last completed successfully, if ever.

last_verified_recipients.description: The recipient set the last verification covered.

last_write_at.description: When the vault object was last successfully written by the backups pod.

last_write_bytes.description: Size (bytes) of the ciphertext from the last successful write.

recipients.description:
Fingerprints of the currently configured recovery recipients (age
public keys).

RecoveryVerifyArgs.description: Answer to an outstanding recovery-verification challenge.

answer.description:
The plaintext obtained by decrypting the challenge from the
`/backups/recovery_challenge` endpoint.

RecoveryVerifyResponse.description: Result of a successful recovery verification.

RedactionGap.description: One server a redacting declaration covers but cannot redact.

server_id.description: The server that would be restored unmasked, and so isn't restored.

version.description: The version it reports, when the reason concerns one.

RedactionGapReason.description:
Why a server a redacting declaration covers can't be redacted.

Each of these withholds the server's worklist entry: a replica that
cannot be redacted is not restored at all, since an unredacted replica
standing in for a redacted one is worse than no replica.

RedactionManifest.description:
Where a type publishes the masking manifests that say how to de-identify a
restored copy of one of its databases.

Canopy holds this rather than the operator: what to mask is a property of
the software, so an operator declaring a redacting replica says only that it
redacts, never where its masking comes from.

artifact_type.description:
The artefact type under which a version's manifest is registered, so
Canopy can tell whether the URL it would hand out has actually been
published for that version.

fallback_to_base.description:
Whether to retry at the `major.minor.0` base version when the versioned
URL 404s, for software publishing per minor rather than per patch.

url_template.description:
Where the manifest for a given version lives. `{version}` is substituted
by the consumer with the version it reads out of the data it restored.

version_query.description:
Single-row, single-column SQL reading the group's own version out of the
restored database, to substitute into `url_template`.

RelatedVersionData.description:
Another patch version within the same release line as a version being
viewed.

RequestArgs.description: Identifies a one-off backup or restore request for a server.

machine_id.description: The box to back up or restore.

purpose.description:
Why this run is requested: `backup` to write new data, or `restore` to
read existing data.

type.description: Backup type to run.

ResolveIncidentArgs.description: Request to mark an incident resolved.

incident_id.description: Identifier of the incident to resolve.

reason.description: Why the incident is considered resolved.

ResolveKnownIssueArgs.description: Identifies a known issue and the version that fixes it.

fix_version.description:
Version string of the first patch that contains the fix. Must be in
the same release line as the issue's earliest affected patch, and
strictly above it.

known_issue_id.description: Id of the known issue to resolve.

resolution_message.description:
Explanation of how or where the issue was fixed. Must not be empty
or whitespace-only.

ResolveTailnetIdentifierArgs.description: A Tailscale identifier to resolve against the live tailnet directory.

identifier.description: A Tailscale IP address, node id, or DNS name to look up.

ResolveTailnetIdentifierResponse.description: Result of resolving a Tailscale identifier.

oneOf.description:
The resolved node's live details, or null if the identifier
didn't match any node in the tailnet.

ResolvedReason.description:
Reason an issue or incident was resolved by an operator.

Stored as text in Postgres, validated as this enum at the API layer.
Categories follow common operational practice (PagerDuty/Sentry/Opsgenie):

- `Fixed` — the underlying problem was addressed.
- `WontFix` — won't fix; not worth doing, or not actually a problem.
- `Expected` — known/expected behaviour (e.g. planned maintenance window).
- `Duplicate` — a duplicate of another issue.
- `Flapping` — too noisy; suppressed rather than fixed (often paired with
  a snooze).
- `Decommissioned` — the check itself was retired fleet-wide; its states
  are resolved as a side effect, not by an operator addressing them.

RestoreActivity.description:
One row of the restore-activity view: either a consumer-reported restore
health check, or a restore inferred from a credential issuance that never
reported (in flight, or terminated without a report). Mirrors the backup
recent-runs view on the restore side.

at.description:
Effective time for sorting/display: the report's observed time when
reported, otherwise the issuance start.

duration_seconds.description:
Canopy-measured restore duration in seconds (report received time minus
first-issuance time). `None` for an in-flight/unreported row or a check
with no matching issuance.

error.description: Error detail for a failed reported restore, if any.

health_details.description: Consumer-supplied health data, if any (reported checks only).

intent.description: The restore intent, when reported. Absent for inferred rows.

key.description:
Stable identity for UI keying: `check-<id>` for a reported check, or
`issuance-<id>` for an inferred restore.

machine_id.description:
The machine the restore is for, when reported. Absent for inferred rows
(the issuance is minted per group+type, not per machine).

observed_at.description:
When the consumer observed the restore result (client-reported); reported
checks only.

outcome.description: The restore outcome; only present for a reported check.

postgres_version.description: PostgreSQL version of the restored database, if reported.

redaction_columns_masked.description: How many columns the manifest masked.

redaction_columns_skipped.description: How many columns it named but could not mask.

redaction_error.description: Why the redaction failed, when it did.

redaction_manifest_version.description: The version whose manifest was fetched.

redaction_outcome.description:
How far the replica's masking manifest got, for a replica that
redacts: `complete`, `partial`, or `failed`.

replica_healthy.description: Whether the restored replica came up healthy; only for a reported check.

reported_at.description: When the consumer's report was received. `None` for an inferred row.

s3_received_payload_bytes.description: Payload bytes received from S3 during the restore, if reported.

s3_received_raw_bytes.description: Raw bytes received from S3 during the restore, if reported.

s3_sent_payload_bytes.description: Payload bytes sent to S3 during the restore, if reported.

s3_sent_raw_bytes.description: Raw bytes sent to S3 during the restore, if reported.

snapshot_id.description: The snapshot that was restored, if reported.

started_at.description:
When the restore started, taken from its matching credential issuance.
`None` when no issuance could be matched.

status.description: Reported, in-flight, or an unreported terminated restore.

type.description: The backup type restored.

RestoreConsumerView.description:
A restore consumer and the restore intents it currently advertises.

A restore consumer is a device with the `backup-restore` role: an agent
that restores backups onto standby replicas. Each advertised intent
carries a description, semantics flags, and a parameter schema, which
together determine what declarations can be created for the consumer and
what parameters they accept.

intents.description: The intents the consumer currently advertises support for.

name.description: Display name of the consumer device, if known.

RestoreReplicaView.description:
A managed-restore declaration, as shown to operators.

A declaration instructs a restore consumer to maintain a restored replica
of a backup, for a given purpose (intent). It also grants the consumer
read access to the covered backups while it is enabled.

can_redact.description:
True when the intent carries the `redact` semantic, so the declaration
can be switched to redacting.

consumer_device_id.description: Identifier of the restore consumer device the declaration is assigned to.

consumer_name.description: Display name of the consumer device, if known.

created_by.description: Login of the operator who created the declaration, if recorded.

enabled.description:
Whether the declaration is active. Disabled declarations are not
dispatched to the consumer and grant no backup access.

gap.description:
True when the consumer does not currently advertise this declaration's
intent, so the declaration is not being dispatched.

group_id.description: Identifier of the server group whose backups the declaration covers.

intent.description:
How the replica is handled, as defined by the consumer: an arbitrary
identifier from the consumer's advertised intents, e.g. `verify`.

machine_id.description:
Specific machine within the group, or null to cover all current machines
in the group.

name.description: Operator-chosen display name for the declaration.

overdue_after.description:
Overdue bound as a human-friendly duration (e.g. `2h 30m` or `1d`):
how long the replica may go without a healthy restore report (or, for
at-most-once intents, how long the latest snapshot may go unverified)
before it is considered overdue. Null means no bound. The same format
is accepted back by `create` and `update`.

params.description:
Operator-supplied parameter values (name → value). Values of
`duration` and `bytes` parameters are formatted as human-friendly
strings (e.g. `2h 30m`, `20Gi`) when the intent's schema is known;
`create` and `update` accept these strings back.

redaction_gaps.description:
Servers this declaration covers that cannot currently be redacted:
either their product publishes no masking manifest, or the version
they report has none published. Each is withheld from the worklist
rather than restored unmasked. Empty unless the declaration redacts.

redacts.description: Whether the replica is served de-identified.

type.description: The backup type to restore, for example `tamanu-postgres`.

updated_at.description: When the declaration was last modified.

RestoreReplicasCreateArgs.description:
Request to declare a new managed restore replica.

The consumer, group, server, backup type, and intent define the
declaration's scope; all of it can be changed later via `update`.

consumer_device_id.description: Identifier of the restore consumer device to assign the declaration to.

group_id.description: Identifier of the server group whose backups to restore.

intent.description:
How the replica is handled, as defined by the consumer: an arbitrary
identifier from the consumer's advertised intents, e.g. `verify`.

machine_id.description:
Specific machine within the group; omit or null to cover all current
machines in the group.

name.description:
Display name for the declaration, unique among the consumer's
declarations.

overdue_after.description:
Overdue bound as a human-friendly duration (jiff's "friendly" format,
e.g. `2h 30m`, `36h`, `1d 12h`); omit, null, or blank for no bound.

params.description:
Parameter values for the intent (name → value), validated against the
consumer's advertised parameter schema. `duration` and `bytes`
parameters accept human-unit strings (e.g. `2h 30m`, `20Gi`) as well
as raw integer seconds/bytes. Defaults to empty.

redacts.description:
Whether the replica is served de-identified. Accepted only for an
intent carrying the `redact` semantic; Canopy resolves the masking
manifest itself from the server's product, so there is nothing else
to set. Defaults to false.

type.description: The backup type to restore, for example `tamanu-postgres`.

RestoreReplicasGroupArgs.description: Scopes a request to one server group.

server_group_id.description: Identifier of the server group.

RestoreReplicasUpdateArgs.description:
Request to update an existing declaration.

Replaces every field, including scope: the consumer, group, server,
backup type, and intent can all be changed in the same call as the name,
overdue bound, parameter values, and enabled flag. Only a name already used
by another of the consumer's declarations maps to `409`; the scope may
match another declaration's.

consumer_device_id.description: Identifier of the restore consumer device to assign the declaration to.

enabled.description: Whether the declaration should be active.

group_id.description: Identifier of the server group whose backups to restore.

id.description: Identifier of the declaration to update.

intent.description:
How the replica is handled, as defined by the consumer: an arbitrary
identifier from the consumer's advertised intents, e.g. `verify`.

machine_id.description:
Specific machine within the group; omit or null to cover all current
machines in the group.

name.description:
New display name for the declaration, unique among the consumer's
declarations.

overdue_after.description:
New overdue bound as a human-friendly duration (jiff's "friendly"
format, e.g. `2h 30m`, `36h`, `1d 12h`); null or blank removes the
bound.

params.description:
New parameter values (name → value), validated against the intent's
advertised parameter schema. `duration` and `bytes` parameters accept
human-unit strings (e.g. `2h 30m`, `20Gi`) as well as raw integer
seconds/bytes. Defaults to empty.

redacts.description:
Whether the replica is served de-identified. Accepted only for an
intent carrying the `redact` semantic. Defaults to false.

type.description: The backup type to restore, for example `tamanu-postgres`.

RestoreWindowRow.description: A machine's currently-open restore window, as shown in the group stats.

allowed_by.description: Who opened the window (Tailscale login), if known.

allowed_until.description:
When the window closes; the machine may mint restore credentials until
then.

machine_id.description: The machine the window applies to.

RestoreWindowView.description: A single machine's restore-window state, for the machine detail page.

allowed_by.description: Who opened the current window (Tailscale login), if known.

allowed_until.description:
When the restore window closes, or `null` if restores are not currently
allowed for this machine.

RetentionPolicy.description:
How many backups to keep at each retention tier once older snapshots are
pruned. The organization enforces minimum floors (at least 7 daily, 4
weekly, and 6 monthly) on write, unless the containing schedule or default
explicitly opts out via its `allow_below_floor` flag.

keep_annual.description:
Number of most-recent annual backups to keep. Defaults to 0 (no annual
retention).

keep_daily.description:
Number of most-recent daily backups to keep. Must be at least 7 unless
the retention floor is bypassed.

keep_latest.description:
Number of most-recent backups to always keep regardless of age.
Defaults to 1.

keep_monthly.description:
Number of most-recent monthly backups to keep. Must be at least 6
unless the retention floor is bypassed.

keep_weekly.description:
Number of most-recent weekly backups to keep. Must be at least 4 unless
the retention floor is bypassed.

RevocationReason.description:
Why a certificate was revoked. The names are the RFC 5280 reasons an
authority accepts; Canopy offers the few an operator would actually reach
for rather than the whole set.

RevokeArgs.description: Request body for revoking an MCP access token.

id.description: The id of the token to revoke.

RunOutcome.description: Outcome of a reported backup or restore run.

RunProgressArgs.description: Identifies the run whose progress series to fetch.

run_id.description: The run identifier, as carried on the activity row (`run_id`).

RunProgressPoint.description:
One point of a run's progress series.

A trimmed projection of what the device reported: the counters a rate or
volume chart plots, and nothing else. The full sample — including whatever the
engine reported that Canopy does not model — is on the activity row's live
figures for a run still in flight.

bytes_cached.description: Cumulative bytes found already present at this point.

bytes_estimated.description: The run's expected total as of this point. May grow over the series.

bytes_hashed.description: Cumulative bytes processed at this point.

bytes_read.description: Cumulative source bytes read at this point.

bytes_uploaded.description: Cumulative bytes uploaded at this point.

s3_received_payload_bytes.description: Cumulative payload bytes received from object storage at this point.

s3_received_raw_bytes.description: Cumulative raw bytes received from object storage at this point.

s3_sent_payload_bytes.description: Cumulative payload bytes sent to object storage at this point.

s3_sent_raw_bytes.description: Cumulative raw bytes sent to object storage at this point.

RunStatus.description:
State of an activity row: a device-reported run, or a run inferred from a
credential issuance that never matched a report.

SampleArgs.description: Request body identifying which healthcheck to sample data for.

namespace.description:
Which catalog entry is meant, as returned in the entry's `namespace`.
Omitted is the unqualified namespace a curated source's checks live in.

source.description:
The source that reports the check. A check's identity is the
(source, check) pair; another source's same-named check may carry
entirely different fields.

SaveArgs.description:
Request body for creating a new snippet, or saving a new version of an
existing one.

description.description: Optional description of what the snippet does.

name.description: The snippet's display name.

sql.description: The SQL query text to store.

supersedes.description:
When set, this save creates a new version that supersedes the
snippet with this id (an edit to an existing snippet). When
omitted, a brand new snippet is created.

ScheduleView.description: A schedule and retention override for one backup type of a server group.

allow_below_floor.description:
Whether this override is allowed to fall below the organization's
minimum retention floor.

expected_interval.description:
Expected seconds between scheduled backups of this type; null means
manual-only (no schedule), which is distinct from an interval of zero.

oneOf.description:
Retention policy override; null means inherit the canopy-wide default
for this backup type.

type.description: Backup type this override applies to.

SelfAlertView.description:
A self-alert: a problem with canopy's own operation, such as an
expiring credential or a failed notification delivery — distinct from
issues raised against monitored applications.

active.description:
Whether the underlying condition is still ongoing. Becomes `false`
once the condition has cleared on its own, independently of whether
an operator has resolved the alert.

detail.description:
Whatever structured detail the condition attached, or `null` where it
attached none. A message is for reading and this is for acting on: the
stale-healthcheck alert, for one, lists the checks it names here so the
surface can link each to its own policy page.

effective_result.description: What policy made of it — the result canopy acts on.

escalates.description:
Whether this condition's policy escalates: an effective failure
notifies immediately, bypassing incident grace.

first_seen.description: When this condition was first raised.

last_seen.description: When this condition was most recently reaffirmed as still ongoing.

message.description: Full detail message describing the condition.

observed_result.description: What canopy observed on the latest raise, before policy.

ref.description:
The stable identifier of the underlying condition, e.g.
`mcp-token-expiry`. Stable across repeated raises of the same
condition.

resolved_at.description:
When an operator marked this alert resolved, or `null` if it has not
been resolved.

resolved_by.description:
The login of the operator who resolved this alert, or `null` if it
has not been resolved.

SelfAlertsResolveArgs.description: Request body for resolving a self-alert.

id.description: The id of the self-alert to resolve.

ServerDataUpdate.description:
Partial update to a server's fields. Only fields present in the request
are changed. For `group_id`, `public_name`, `cloud`, and `geolocation`,
sending an explicit `null` clears the field, while omitting it leaves the
current value unchanged.

alert_when_down_for.description:
New downtime threshold in seconds before this server is considered
down. Omit to leave unchanged.

cloud.description:
Whether the server runs in a cloud environment, or `null` to clear.
Omit to leave unchanged.

oneOf.description:
New geographic location for the server, or `null` to clear it. Omit
to leave unchanged.

group_id.description:
New group for the server, or `null` to remove it from its group.
Omit to leave unchanged.

host.description:
New URL for the server. An empty string clears it; omit to leave
unchanged.

is_monitored.description:
Whether canopy should actively monitor this server. Omit to leave
unchanged.

may_manage_dns.description:
Whether this server may manage its own DNS records for names under its
group's domains. Omit to leave unchanged.

may_manage_tls.description:
Whether this server may obtain TLS certificates for names under its
group's domains. Omit to leave unchanged.

name.description: New name for the server. Omit to leave unchanged.

notes.description: New free-text notes for the server. Omit to leave unchanged.

public_name.description:
New public-facing name for the server, or `null` to unlist it. Omit
to leave unchanged.

oneOf.description: New promotion rank for the server. Omit to leave unchanged.

New set of operator-defined tags for the server. Omit to leave
unchanged.

ServerDetailData.description:
Full detail view of a server: its own record, its bound device, its most
recent status report, current reachability/health, and group context.

billing_labels.description:
The server's own effective `billing.*` labels
(product/deployment/stage) — the ones canopy hands the server's device,
carrying its own product and rank rather than its group's. Empty when
the server is ungrouped, there being no group to attribute to.

checks.description:
The server's current checks across every source, graded and
classified — the live consolidated checks view.

oneOf.description: Full detail on the device bound to this server, if any.

The group this server belongs to, with its notes/tags so the UI can
render the "Group" section without a second fetch. `None` when the
server is ungrouped.

group_applications.description:
Every application in the group, this one included, for the tree the page
ends with. Empty when the application is ungrouped. Each entry carries
its own `up` / `health` so the tree renders a status dot per workload.

group_machines.description:
Every machine in the group, for the same tree: the boxes the
applications above are arranged under. Empty when the application is
ungrouped.

health.description: Current self-reported health, derived from the most recent status report.

oneOf.description: The server's most recently reported status, if it has ever reported one.

machine_name.description:
The name of the box this application runs on, where it has one.

The page names its machine in the heading, so it needs the name and not
only the id `server.machine_id` carries — and it needs it whether or
not the application is grouped, which is why it is not read out of
`group_machines`.

maintained.description:
Whether a maintenance window suspends this server, its own or its
group's: its checks are recorded and shown, and raise nothing.

maintenance_settling.description:
Whether the suspension is only the settle period: the window has
ended and watching resumes when it elapses.

up.description: Current reachability, derived from the most recent status report.

ServerGroup.description:
A group of applications managed together: incidents roll up across the group,
members share tags, and the group carries its own notes and
notification settings.

deleted_at.description:
When set, the group is archived: hidden from live listings but kept,
along with its members, and can be restored.

oneOf.description:
The version reported by the group's canonical member server. `None`
if the group has no members or that member hasn't reported a
version yet.

name.description: The group's display name.

notes.description: Free-form operator notes about this group.

slack_close_delay.description:
How long, in seconds, an incident lingers after its last failure
recovers before it closes and the resolved notification is sent. A
failure returning within this window continues the same incident
instead of opening (and notifying about) a new one — the close-side
mirror of `slack_open_delay`, for a red check that briefly blips
green.

slack_open_delay.description:
How long, in seconds, an incident-opened notification waits before
it's sent. If the incident resolves within this window, the
notification is cancelled outright and never sent — useful for
groups prone to brief flapping, so a transient blip doesn't spam
notifications, without losing the underlying incident record.

tags.description: Key/value tags shared by every server in the group.

updated_at.description: When this group was last modified.

version_application_id.description:
The id of the group's canonical member server (the one whose version
is reflected in `effective_version`), chosen by highest rank then
highest kind. `None` when the group has no members.

ServerGroupCard.description:
A status-dashboard card summarising one group of equivalent servers, with
a status entry per member. The group's version is taken from whichever
member reported most recently.

all_members_quiet.description:
Whether every member of the group has been quiet for long enough that
archiving the group cascades to them.

This is the archive rule, not a reachability reading: a member that
last reported months ago is thoroughly unreachable but has still
reported, so `up` alone cannot answer it. Both this and the rule the
archive itself enforces ask the same question of the same window, so
the button offered and the outcome cannot disagree.

members.description: Status of each server belonging to this group.

oneOf.description:

version_distance.description:

incidents and notifications.

created_by.description: The operator who created this silence. `None` if not recorded.

namespace.description:

application types, so two of them reporting one check name are two

notes.description: Free-form notes about the group. Defaults to empty.

slack_close_delay.description:

open after its last failure recovers, so a failure returning within
the window continues the same incident instead of opening (and
notifying about) a new one. Omit to accept the default.

slack_open_delay.description:
Optional initial delay, in whole seconds, before an "incident opened"
Slack notification for this group is delivered; an incident that

address, monitoring configuration, and (when requested by the endpoint)

alert_when_down_for.description:
Threshold in seconds for the reachability sweep to consider this
server down. Always positive; only consulted when `is_monitored`
is `true`. The default at creation is 600 (10 minutes).

cloud.description: Whether this server runs in a cloud environment, if known.

display_host.description:

hostname}` when the server has no URL but runs on a machine bound to a

oneOf.description: Geographic location of the server, if known.

group_id.description: The group this server belongs to, if any.

machine_id.description:

maintained.description:

decorate listings; `None` where they aren't.

may_manage_dns.description:

may_manage_tls.description:

name.description: Operator-assigned name for the server, if any.

notes.description: Free-text operator notes about the server.

public_name.description:

oneOf.description:

tags.description: Arbitrary operator-defined key/value labels attached to the server.

type.description:

oneOf.description:

report. Omitted when the endpoint that produced this response didn't
batch-fetch statuses (e.g. the cheap list/get endpoints); a present
value of "gone" means the lookup ran and found no status at all.

bestool.description:

source reports one.

extra.description: Additional endpoint-defined data included with this status push.

id.description: Unique identifier for this status report.

min_chrome_version.description:

version, if determinable.

nodejs.description: Node.js version associated with the server, if known.

operators.description:

timezone.description: Timezone the server reported, if any.

type.description:

version_distance.description:

The profile, as the authority names it, or null for the authority's own

Request to set (or override) the schedule and retention for one backup
type of a server group.

allow_below_floor.description:
Allows this override to specify retention below the organization's
minimum retention floor. Defaults to false.

expected_interval.description:
Expected seconds between scheduled backups of this type; null means
manual-only (no schedule), which is distinct from an interval of zero.

oneOf.description:
Retention policy to apply; null means inherit the canopy-wide default
for this backup type. A specified policy is validated against the
organization's minimum retention floor unless `allow_below_floor` is
set.

server_group_id.description: The server group to configure.

type.description: Backup type this schedule and retention apply to.

ingest.description: The ingest mode to apply: `allow`, `ignore`, or `deny`.

source.description:
The source to configure. The reserved `canopy`/`manual` names are
rejected.

reachability.description: The reachability mode to apply: `on`, `quiet`, or `off`.

source.description:
The source to configure. The reserved `canopy`/`manual` names are
rejected.

SetTypeDefaultArgs.description:
Request to set the canopy-wide default schedule and retention for a
backup type.

allow_below_floor.description:
Allows this default to specify retention below the organization's

auto_enable.description:
Whether a server's capability for this type should be enabled by

default_interval.description: Seconds between scheduled runs; null = manual-only.

default_retention.description: Default retention policy for this type.

type.description: Backup type these defaults apply to.

ShortStatus.description:
Reachability of a target, from how recently it last reported.

Three states and no degrees between them: a target is reachable,
unreachable, or has never reported. How long it has been quiet is measured
against that target's own configured threshold rather than any fixed one, so
a target that reports every few minutes and one that reports hourly are
each judged on what is normal for them.

SilenceGroupArgs.description:
Request body identifying an issue to silence (or unsilence) across a
whole server group.

application_type.description:
Which application type's check is meant, for a check named by an
application rather than by a box. A group covers several types, so the
caller names the one it is silencing from; `null` is a machine's check
or a curated source's.

ref.description: The specific issue identifier within `source` to silence.

server_group_id.description: The server group to silence the issue on.

source.description:
Identifies what raises the issue being silenced — for example a
specific healthcheck or backup pipeline.

Request body identifying an issue to silence (or unsilence) on a single

ref.description: The specific issue identifier within `source` to silence.

source.description:
Identifies what raises the issue being silenced — for example a
specific healthcheck.

SilenceServerArgs.description:
Request body identifying an issue to silence (or unsilence) on a

ref.description: The specific issue identifier within `source` to silence.

Identifies what raises the issue being silenced — for example a

SnapshotArgs.description: Selects a server and a point in time to fetch a status snapshot for.

Point in time the snapshot should be "as of". Returns the most

`null`) to get the latest status with no time bound.

SourceData.description:
One reporting source with its reachability policy and fleet-wide
last-seen.

ingest.description:
Whether the device API ingests this source's reports: `allow`,
`ignore` (accepted but discarded), or `deny` (rejected). A source
that isn't ingested is excluded from reachability.

last_seen.description:
When any of this source's checks was most recently reported anywhere
in the fleet. `null` until liveness has been reconciled.

reachability.description:
How this source's silence bears on its applications' reachability: `on`
(a stale source warns, all-stale is unreachable), `quiet` (never
warns, still counts toward unreachable), or `off` (excluded).

source.description: The source name, as reported by devices.

SqlHistoryEntry.description: One entry in the shared history of queries run in the SQL playground.

id.description: Unique identifier for this history entry.

query.description: The SQL text that was executed.

tailscale_user.description: Tailscale login of the user who ran the query.

SqlQuery.description:
A single SQL statement to run, as submitted to (or replayed from) the
read-only SQL playground.

SqlResult.description: The result of running a query in the read-only SQL playground.

columns.description:
Column names, in the order they appear in each row. Empty if the
query returned no rows.

execution_time_ms.description:
How long the query took to run, in milliseconds. Timing starts
immediately before the query is sent and stops once every value
has been read back, including any text conversions.

Endpoint overhead is deliberately outside the window: both pool
checkouts, the write to the shared history, and the transaction
setup. Those are not what the operator is measuring when they time
a query, and the read-only pool's checkout in particular can
dominate under contention.

rows.description:
The result rows. Each row is a list of values positionally
aligned with `columns`. Most Postgres types are converted to
their natural JSON equivalent (numbers, booleans, strings,
timestamps as strings, nested JSON, arrays). Types without a
natural JSON equivalent — money, ranges, and geometric types, for
example — are rendered as their text representation instead, and
so is a genuine SQL NULL, which appears here as the literal
string `"NULL"` rather than a JSON null. A JSON `null` in this
data means the value couldn't be converted at all.

StabilityData.description:
A state's full stability record on the wire: the stored counters, ring,
and profile, plus the derived statistics. Shared by the private API and
the MCP interface.

degraded_observations.description: How many of them were degraded (observed warning/failed/broken).

duty_cycle.description:
Hour-of-week degradation profile: 168 buckets, UTC, Monday 00:00
first, each with how many observations landed there and how many
were degraded. Recent-leaning: bucket counters halve at a cap.

last_observed_at.description: When the state was last observed (skipped observations excluded).

last_observed_degraded.description: Whether the last observation was degraded.

observations.description: Total observations recorded for this state.

stats.description: Statistics derived from the transition ring.

transitions.description: The remembered healthy↔degraded transitions, oldest first.

StabilityStats.description: Flap statistics derived from a transition ring.

flips_24h.description: State changes recorded in the last 24 hours.

flips_7d.description: State changes recorded in the last 7 days.

ring_covers_from.description:
The oldest remembered transition: the flip counts only see back to
here, so on a heavily flapping state they are lower bounds.

typical_degraded_run_secs.description:
Median length of the completed degraded runs the ring remembers,
in seconds.

typical_healthy_gap_secs.description:
Median length of the completed healthy gaps between remembered
degraded runs, in seconds.

StatusSnapshotData.description:
A single status push from a server, as of a point in time, with derived
health and version information.

bestool.description:
Version of bestool, the agent reporting on the server. Absent when no
source reports one.

checks.description:
The server's consolidated checks as of this snapshot: every source's
checks, graded and classified, with silenced flags and the rolled-up
health state — the same shape the live view uses.

created_at.description: When this status push was recorded.

device_id.description: Id of the device that sent this status push, if known.

extra.description:
Additional unstructured data reported alongside the snapshot, keyed
by source (`{ [source]: { …fields } }`) so a multi-source snapshot's
raw payloads stay attributed rather than merged. Sources whose
payload is empty are omitted.

id.description: Unique identifier for this status push.

min_chrome_version.description:
Minimum embedded browser version required by this software version,
if known.

operators.description:
Operators identified as connected to the server as of this push,
with display name and profile picture filled in where known. Not
filtered by recency — reflects this specific point-in-time snapshot.

reporting_schema.description:
Version the server's reporting schema was built for. Absent until a
server runs a schema that stamps one (spec: RPT#the-offering-contract).

server_id.description: Id of the server this status was reported by.

type.description:
The application the server runs. Travels with the version so a
consumer can tell a product with no version from one that has yet to
report one.

oneOf.description: Software version reported in this push.

version_distance.description:
How many releases behind the latest published version this push's
version is. Absent when there's no published version to compare
against.

SubmitManualEventArgs.description: A manually raised condition to record against a server.

active.description:
Whether the underlying condition is currently active. Defaults to
`true` when omitted; `false` records it as cleared regardless of
`result`.

applicationId.description: Id of the server the condition applies to.

description.description:
Short, single-line headline for the condition. Must not contain
newlines — use `message` for multi-line detail.

escalates.description:
Whether the condition's failures should notify immediately,
bypassing the incident grace period. Only consulted the first time
a `ref` is seen (it seeds the condition's catalog entry); adjust
later from the healthchecks catalog.

message.description: Human-readable message describing the condition. May be multi-line.

ref.description:
Identifier for the underlying condition. Reports with the same
`ref` on the same server update the same issue rather than opening
a new one each time; use a fresh unique value if that deduplication
isn't wanted.

oneOf.description:
The condition's result: `failed` (can open an incident) or
`warning` (context only). Defaults to `failed`. `passed` records
the condition as cleared, same as `active: false`.

bracket.description:

server.

releases.description:

production, each as a `[major, minor]` pair.

versions.description:
Every distinct full version string currently observed in
production, in ascending order.

network, fetched from the cached tailnet directory rather than stored
on the device record itself.

addresses.description: The node's current Tailscale IP addresses.

display_name.description: The node's display name in the Tailscale admin console.

last_seen.description:
When the Tailscale network last saw this node online. Omitted if
that information wasn't available.

node_id.description: The Tailscale network's unique identifier for this node.

same heuristic Tailscale's own admin console uses to mark a node

tailnet.description: The tailnet (Tailscale network) this node belongs to.
